title: Sorting Bible Concepts: Early Christian Themes
prompt: Sort the following Bible-related terms into categories based on their meanings and roles. Some terms may belong to more than one category. Use the categories to help you understand how these concepts connect.

title: Review of Key Bible Concepts
prompt: Choose the best answer for each question about important Bible concepts.

items.prompt: What does the term 'gospel' primarily refer to in the Bible?
options: The good news about Jesus Christ

items.prompt: Which Gospels are called 'synoptic' because they share a similar viewpoint?
In biblical times, who would be considered an 'outcast'?
What does 'certainty' mean when reading the Bible?
options: Confidence in the truth of the message

title: Exploring Incarnation and Praise Through Photography
prompt: Take a photo of something that represents the concept of 'incarnation' from the Bible, such as a symbol or scene that shows God becoming human. Then, find or create an image that shows 'praise,' like people expressing gratitude or worship. In your caption, explain why you chose these images and how they help you understand the ideas of incarnation and praise in the Bible. Write 2–4 sentences connecting your photos to these concepts.

title: Bible Concepts Review: Spot the Real Answer!
prompt: Read each question carefully and choose the real answer. Watch out for the silly joke option trying to trick you!

rounds.prompt: In the Bible, what is a disciple?
options: A follower of Jesus who learns from him
A leader of a lost and found department
A superhero with a cape and sandals
rounds.jokeOption: A superhero with a cape and sandals
rounds.correctOption: A follower of Jesus who learns from him

rounds.prompt: What does the parable of 'lost and found' teach us?
options: That lost socks always find their way home
God's joy when a sinner returns
How to organize lost items in a temple
rounds.jokeOption: That lost socks always find their way home
rounds.correctOption: God's joy when a sinner returns

rounds.prompt: What is meant by 'reversal' in many Bible stories?
options: A new way to tie sandals
A change where the humble are lifted up
rounds.correctOption: A change where the humble are lifted up

rounds.prompt: What does 'universal' mean in the Bible context?
options: Something that applies to all people everywhere
A spaceship that visits all planets
rounds.jokeOption: A spaceship that visits all planets
rounds.correctOption: Something that applies to all people everywhere

rounds.prompt: What does 'certainty' refer to in faith?
options: Knowing the lottery numbers in advance
The exact date of the Bible's writing
rounds.jokeOption: Knowing the lottery numbers in advance

title: Joyful Prayer Stretch
prompt: Stand up tall and take a deep breath. Raise your arms high above your head as you think about a joyful prayer. Slowly bend forward to touch your toes, then rise back up stretching your arms wide like you're embracing joy. Repeat this stretch two more times, breathing deeply and feeling thankful.

title: Feed the Pet: Bible Concepts Review
prompt: Feed your pet only the TRUE statements about Bible concepts! Avoid the false ones or your pet will get sick!
goodFoods: The gospel means 'good news' about Jesus Christ.
Disciples were followers who learned from Jesus.
The resurrection refers to Jesus rising from the dead.
Gentiles are non-Jewish people mentioned in the Bible.
Parables are stories Jesus told to teach moral lessons.
The Holy Spirit is described as God's guiding presence.
badFoods: The gospel is a type of ancient musical instrument.
Tax collectors were the most popular people in biblical times.
Pharisees were known for breaking all the religious laws.
The kingdom of God refers to a physical castle in Jerusalem.
Theophilus was the name of a famous Roman emperor.

title: Synthesizing Key Concepts from the Bible
prompt: Read the following points carefully. Then write a 3–5 sentence synthesis that includes a clear claim and evidence using all the concepts: good news, messiah, sinners, women, and certainty.

prompts: The Bible shares the good news that the messiah came to save sinners and offer hope to all people.
Women played important roles in spreading the message and witnessing the life of the messiah.
Believers have certainty in the promises given through the messiah, which brings comfort and faith.
The good news emphasizes forgiveness and salvation, showing that even sinners are welcomed.

title: Sequencing Key Events in Early Christianity
prompt: Put the following events in the correct chronological order based on Bible history.

items: Old Testament prophecies about the Messiah written (circa 700 BC)
John the Baptist begins preaching in the wilderness (circa 26 AD)
Jesus calls his first disciples to follow him (circa 27 AD)
Jesus teaches the Parable of the Lost Son (circa 29 AD)
Jesus is crucified and resurrected in Jerusalem (circa 30 AD)
The Holy Spirit comes at Pentecost and the early Church begins (circa 30 AD)

title: Sharing Our Understanding: Bible Concepts Review
prompt: In your team, each member will receive a unique role with a clue about a Bible concept. Share your clues with each other and work together to create one clear explanation that connects all four concepts.

config.scenario: Your team of Bible scholars has been asked to present a brief explanation connecting four key concepts from your studies. Each of you has been given one concept to research. Combine your findings into a unified presentation.

roles.name: Holy Spirit Scholar
roles.goal: Explain how the Holy Spirit guides and comforts believers
roles.constraint: You must connect the Holy Spirit to at least one other team member's concept

roles.name: Poverty & Justice Researcher
roles.goal: Explain the Bible's teachings about caring for the poor
roles.constraint: Reference a specific parable or teaching about the poor

roles.name: Testimony Witness
roles.goal: Explain what testimony means and why personal faith stories matter
roles.constraint: Give an example of how testimony strengthens a community

roles.name: Certainty Defender
roles.goal: Explain what certainty in faith means and how believers find confidence
roles.constraint: Connect certainty to at least one of the other three concepts
